title: A visual tool astronauts use to assess their own health and act on its status: the screens
done_when: On one screen the astronaut sees the status of each indicator they track and a clear next step; content comes from config/ (REQ-26)

title: Gather health indicators from user input: keyboard and clicks; camera or images are optional
done_when: Every chosen indicator can be entered without special hardware; units shown at entry

title: Confirm each chosen indicator is measurable on board, and how
done_when: For each indicator the team chose (T-06): instrument or method in flight, unit and precision, with a NASA or peer-reviewed source; any statement example left out (for example blood sugar) says why, in docs/DECISIONS.md through Wambi
source: CS: Challenge statement · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/health-monitoring-software/ (background: blood pressure, heart rate, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep hours, mood)

title: Each indicator answers the five questions of the statement, assembled in one place
done_when: Per indicator: question 2 (why it is needed) written by Bio 1 with sources, and links to the answers of questions 1 (REQ-03), 3 (REQ-07), 4 (REQ-05) and 5 (REQ-06)

title: Say when a result needs attention from the crew, the CMO or the flight surgeon
done_when: Each indicator has an attention rule with its source, or the rule is labelled Assumption in the interface

title: Guidance on treatments and health improvement; possible conditions as probabilities, never a certainty
done_when: Every attention state shows what to do; a suggested condition shows its probability, what it is based on and that the CMO or flight surgeon confirms; no "you have X" anywhere

title: Explain how the five spaceflight hazards affect what is measured
done_when: Each indicator names the hazards that affect it (radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, hostile closed environments) with a NASA source

title: Simple instructions on measurements, indicators and risks; no assumed expertise
done_when: Numbered steps, one action per sentence; Bio 2 reviews every text for plain language

title: Optional considerations chosen or left out on purpose
done_when: Human figure, colour coding, dynamic charts, routine prompts, gamification, mission environments, animations and camera input each have a row in docs/DECISIONS.md: use or leave out, and why (decided by the team in T-06)
source: CS: Challenge statement · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/health-monitoring-software/ (objectives and potential considerations)

title: Every medical statement has a source or is marked Assumption, visible to the user: review
done_when: Bio 2 reviews config/ and the interface before each checkpoint; no unsourced statement remains; Assumption labels show in the app

title: Never presented as a replacement for the CMO or the flight surgeon
done_when: Interface, pitch and page say the tool supports the crew's own assessment and that decisions stay with the CMO and flight surgeon
source: Our: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C · https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/nasa-std-3001-vol-1-rev-c-with-signature.pdf ([V1 3004] in-mission medical care)

title: History view: each indicator against the person's own earlier values
done_when: Each indicator has a history view comparing with that astronaut's own earlier values, reading the stored history (REQ-27)
source: Our: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C · https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/nasa-std-3001-vol-1-rev-c-with-signature.pdf ([V1 3004] trending vital signs; limits relative to each person's baseline) · CS: Challenge statement · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/health-monitoring-software/ (dynamic charts)

title: Data keeps working with delayed or no contact with Earth
done_when: Entries are saved locally with no network; anything meant for the ground waits in a queue and is sent later without duplicates
source: CS: Challenge statement · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/health-monitoring-software/ (hazard: distance from Earth) · https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/hazard-distance-from-earth/

title: Treat health data as private; no real personal data anywhere
done_when: No real personal data in the repository or the app; the interface labels all data as synthetic. One exception (REQ-36): a face descriptor the person chooses to register stays only in their own browser
source: Our: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C · https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/nasa-std-3001-vol-1-rev-c-with-signature.pdf ([V1 6003] private medical communication)

title: Readable and usable without colour alone or a mouse
done_when: Every state has text or an icon besides colour; the demo path works by keyboard
source: Our: team quality rule (colour coding is a statement consideration)

title: Everything submitted is in English: page and linked materials
done_when: Page, slides and linked documents in English; a video may be spoken in another language only with English subtitles

title: Demo format, script and slides within the limits
done_when: Format chosen (video of 30 s or less, or 7 slides at most including title and intro); script or slides ready and checked against the limit

title: Public repository with a README that explains how to run the project
done_when: Repository public; README says what HeMoSo is and how to run it; opens in a private window with no login

title: Use and name at least one NASA data or resource; list every other data, tool, code and image used
done_when: Page fields NASA Data and Space Agency Partner Data filled from docs/nasa_data.md and docs/sources.md; licences and permissions checked
source: SG: Submission guide · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/resources/project-submission-guide/ (required for global awards)

title: Super Intelligence (SI) use disclosed on the page and in images and video
done_when: The page answers the SI question from team/eng1/notes/si-use-log.md and the people's logs; SI images and video carry a visible watermark; no NASA logos, flags or mission identifiers in generated content
source: SG: Submission guide · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/resources/project-submission-guide/ (Use of Super Intelligence)

title: The pitch answers the five judging criteria
done_when: The script says how HeMoSo serves Impact, Creativity, Validity, Relevance and Presentation

title: No images, video, audio or likeness of people under 18
done_when: Every image and clip checked before upload

title: Submit for judging before the internal freeze
done_when: Terms and originality boxes checked and Submit for Judging pressed by Sun 13:30; official close Sun 15 Nov 23:59 Medellín time
source: SG: Submission guide · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/resources/project-submission-guide/ (submission start and end times)

title: All five members registered for the Medellín event and on the team's Members tab
done_when: Members tab of ReTardis shows all five; no member can be added after submission closes
source: JG: Judging guide · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/resources/judging-awards-guide/ (eligibility: at most six members, same local event)

title: Local judging and the 14:00 mentor presentation confirmed with the local lead
done_when: Time, length and language confirmed and logged (T-04)
source: Local: Medellín event schedule · SG: Submission guide · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/resources/project-submission-guide/ (local judging times may differ)

title: Status and next-step texts the astronaut reads for each indicator
done_when: Every status of every chosen indicator has a short text and a next step in config/, plain words, sourced or marked Assumption

title: Keep each astronaut's measurements over time so earlier values can be compared
done_when: Every entry is stored with time, unit and person; the history survives a reload; a function returns a person's earlier values for an indicator
source: Our: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C · https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/nasa-std-3001-vol-1-rev-c-with-signature.pdf ([V1 3004] trending vital signs; limits relative to each person's baseline) · CS: Challenge statement · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/health-monitoring-software/ (dynamic charts)

title: Interface works offline and shows what is waiting to be sent
done_when: The app opens and works with the network off after the first load; pending items and the last sync time are visible
source: CS: Challenge statement · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/health-monitoring-software/ (hazard: distance from Earth) · https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/hazard-distance-from-earth/

title: Synthetic demo data with its assumptions documented
done_when: The demo dataset in config/data/ is synthetic, each value range has a source or is marked Assumption, and the generation method is written down
source: Our: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C · https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/nasa-std-3001-vol-1-rev-c-with-signature.pdf ([V1 6003] private medical communication)

title: The app interface is in English
done_when: Every screen, label and message of the app in English

title: Demo video recorded with English subtitles and a public link
done_when: Video of 30 s or less recorded from the app, English subtitles burned in, hosted outside Space Apps, link opens with no password, permission or registration

title: Running app published at a public link
done_when: The app opens at a public link in a private window with no login, on desktop and phone

title: SI-assisted code and data acknowledged in the repository
done_when: The solution idea came from the team; SI-assisted code and data are acknowledged in descriptive text and metadata (a file at the repository root built from team/eng1/notes/si-use-log.md)
source: SG: Submission guide · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/resources/project-submission-guide/ (Use of Super Intelligence)

title: The submission page answers the five judging criteria
done_when: The page description says how HeMoSo serves Impact, Creativity, Validity, Relevance and Presentation

title: Two-minute story for the mentors rehearsed three times
done_when: The story is read aloud in two minutes or less, three times, before 14:00 on Sunday
source: Local: Medellín event schedule · SG: Submission guide · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/resources/project-submission-guide/ (local judging times may differ)

title: Sign in with the face, on the device only (optional)
done_when: Shown on the Identify screen (decision Sat 23:25, docs/DECISIONS.md); nothing is downloaded and no camera opens until the person chooses it; the person consents first; a face is registered once and matched in the browser with bundled models; no image or face data leaves the device; the person can delete it; the person picker works without a camera

title: Sign in with a username and a PIN checked on the server; the face unlocks it on a device
done_when: A person creates an account with a username and a 4 to 8 digit PIN; the server stores only a salted scrypt hash; signing in returns a session token and the routes of a person with an account refuse requests without it; the same account works on any device; after one PIN sign-in on a device the face unlocks that stored session (the face data stays on the device, REQ-36); the synthetic demo astronaut opens with one click and no PIN (REQ-32)

title: Reaction check and the current psychological state
done_when: The astronaut can take a short reaction test with a light or a sound; it stores the median reaction time and the lapses as two indicators compared with the person's own baseline; a neuro-behavioural condition joins them with mood and sleep as an evidence score describing the current state, never a label or diagnosis, with the CMO or flight surgeon confirming; offline, keyboard and touch, light-only option
